speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: asked	the Minister for Communications and Information with regard to IDA's requirement that all public servants' computers with Government email capabilities be delinked from the Internet (a) what are the reasons that prompted such a major review; (b) what are the other solutions that have been considered before arriving at the current guidelines; (c) whether inputs from other Ministries and agencies have been sought in terms of its implementation; and (d) what potential impact will the requirement have on the productivity and service delivery of our public servants.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: asked	the Minister for Communications and Information (a) how will the Government help businesses and organisations protect themselves against the threats behind the move to delink Internet access on public servants' computers; (b) whether the move will affect the development of the Smart Nation platform and its pervasive connectivity; and (c) what steps will be taken to restore public confidence in the Smart Nation vision.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In May 2015, I informed Parliament that the Government had detected a security breach in MFA's IT system.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Immediate steps were taken to remove the threat and to remediate affected systems.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Since then, there have been more targeted cyberattacks on Government networks.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: While these attacks were successfully contained, we can expect more to follow.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Cybersecurity firms, such as Mandiant and Microsoft Research, have published reports explaining in detail how such attacks are carried out.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It is clear from these reports that the attackers rely on the Internet to introduce malware into a network, to send instructions to infected machines, to infect more machines within a network and, finally, to steal data from the network.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IDA studied this issue together with the agencies for several years.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: When we spoke to other governments, some indicated that they set up isolated networks, whilst some have explored limiting Internet access only to the necessary functions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Due to security reasons, these measures are generally not publicised.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In the meantime, agencies assessed to be at higher risk, such as MTI and MFA, went ahead with separating Internet surfing.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But agency-level arrangements do not make the whole Government network safer, because an attacker can still enter the network via another agency which continues to allow Internet surfing when connected to the Government network.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Government has a duty to do all it can to protect the data it possesses, especially since such data often contain personal information of our citizens.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It will mean that public officers have to make some changes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: They will now have to access the Internet via a different device, rather than from a single device.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The device that they use for Internet surfing must only be used for unclassified work.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But the key point, Madam, is that they can still surf the Internet for work, using either separate devices provided by their organisation or their own mobile devices.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: They will still be able to send and receive e-mails from Government officers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: There is no reason to believe that the effectiveness of agencies will be adversely affected.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Agencies like MTI and MFA have already implemented the separation of Internet surfing for some years, while MINDEF has implemented even more stringent requirements.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: These organisations have not become less effective as a result.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Cyber Security Agency (CSA) has been working closely with industry associations to promote the importance of cybersecurity.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It has organised conferences with the Singapore Business Federation (SBF) on cybersecurity.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Government worked with SBF to develop an Employee Cyber Security Kit.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This free toolkit features a simple quiz which provides an initial assessment of a company's cybersecurity readiness and follows up with a recommended cybersecurity education programme tailored to meet business needs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: There have been over 3,000 downloads of the resources and tools.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: CSA and the Singapore Infocomm Technology Federation co-chair a Cyber Security Awareness Alliance, which does good work in increasing awareness and adoption of cybersecurity practices.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, help is available to our businesses who want to do something to improve their cybersecurity.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In fact, other countries have expressed interest in learning from our experience.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We cannot be a Smart Nation that is trusted and resilient if our systems are exposed and vulnerable.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I just want to ask the Minister in considering this solution – because some in the industry would consider it quite extreme – were there more elegant solutions that were thought through?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For instance, did they consider tiered networking or a lockdown environment?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The second question is: would the Ministry be looking into what is the productivity impact on civil servants?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For example, today, if I send the Minister an email with a link on it, the Minister would have to email it somewhere else, to another device, just to surf, to know what is this link about, for example.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, there is definitely impact on productivity, even for the simplest of things.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What will the productivity impact be, and will the Ministry be studying the impact on civil servants?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The first answer is yes, we did explore other solutions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I am not at liberty to discuss today in Parliament what solutions we explored because we have a whole range of efforts that we can put in.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For example, the Prime Minister and some Ministers have already gone on with the separation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I have a separate laptop altogether – it allows me to surf the Internet.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So far, it has not affected our work.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: On the issue of productivity, I think this is something which we will continue to monitor.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Certainly, we do not want to affect the work of our public officers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: There is a whole series of workshops that we are conducting with senior management right down to the IT division within each of the Ministries for them to work together and find the best way forward.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I think we recognise that there may be some instances where separation may not be possible now because of the nature of the work.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, we will leave this to the agencies to work with IDA to determine exactly how we are going to proceed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But as a policy, the Government has adopted this as the best way forward for us to ensure that we do not have any more attacks.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: At the same time, you and I know; I cannot promise there will be no more attacks because the hackers are becoming more sophisticated, new hacking tools are being developed and it is always very difficult for us to keep ahead.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, we think this is the best approach going forward.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But like all governments, we will never close off other options.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We will continue to explore what are the available options out there and see whether we will review our strategies down the road.
